quizzes.stem: A team wants to cut the cost of a workload on Claude Opus 5.5 that currently thinks a lot. A developer proposes setting `thinking` to `disabled`. What does the page say?

options.a: The request returns a 400, so remove the output cap instead
options.b: The request succeeds, and thinking stops for that call alone
options.c: The request succeeds, and thinking falls to its lowest setting
options.d: The request returns a 400, so lower the effort level instead

explanation.d: The model table shows "400 error" for `disabled` on Opus 5.5, and the page says to "lower effort first" to cut cost.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 always think adaptively and cannot be told otherwise".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the lowest setting named is Sonnet 5.5's, "up-front thinking off at high effort or below", and Opus 5.5 has no such setting.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "`max_tokens` is a strict limit" on spend and does not change how much the model thinks.

quizzes.stem: A response has a short visible reply and an `output_tokens` of 1,900. The `thinking_tokens` field reads 1,650. What is billed as output?

options.a: All 1,900 tokens, since thinking is charged even when it is not shown
options.b: Only 250 tokens, since the thinking was hidden by the default display
options.c: Only 1,650 tokens, since the answer is covered by the input price
options.d: About 80 tokens, since billing follows the words that are returned

explanation.a: The page says "You are billed for the full thinking process, not the thinking content visible in the response."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the thinking tokens are "billed as output tokens", whether the display shows them or not.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page bills "the full thinking process, not the thinking content visible in the response", so the answer is not the only part charged.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says the visible text understates the bill: "So the visible text understates the bill."

quizzes.stem: A request on Claude Haiku 4.5 puts `low` under `output_config` to save money. What does the page back?

options.a: Haiku 4.5 takes the setting only together with a manual budget
options.b: Haiku 4.5 treats `low` as its default, so the setting changes nothing
options.c: That model has no such control, so the setting buys no saving
options.d: Haiku 4.5 applies the setting to tool calls and ignores thinking

explanation.c: The page says "Haiku 4.5 does not support effort", and the table of effort support lists the other three models.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the default row names only Opus 5.5 and the models that support effort: "The default is high on every model that supports effort except Opus 5.5".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the manual budget belongs to the thinking setting, and the page puts effort "in output_config, not inside thinking".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says effort "works with or without thinking" on models that support it.

quizzes.stem: A chat feature on Opus 5.5 streams long answers to people watching the text appear, and the team wants it to arrive sooner without a change of tier or effort. Which option does the page support?

options.a: Fast mode, at the standard price and on every cloud platform
options.b: Fast mode, at twice the standard price and on the first-party API only
options.c: A lower effort level, with a reduced price and shorter replies
options.d: A batch, at half the price and with the replies delivered sooner

explanation.b: The page says fast mode "is available on the Claude API (first-party) only" and prices it at twice the standard rate.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "it is not available on Claude Platform on AWS or partner-operated cloud platforms".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the table gives "fast mode (Opus only)" to streaming, and gives lowering the effort to "Too slow to finish".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Fast mode is not available with the Batch API."

quizzes.stem: A tool loop runs four calls for one user question. The team sets reasoning on for the first call and off for the last three to save tokens. What happens?

options.a: The API treats each call as its own turn and accepts the new setting
options.b: The API returns a 400 for the first changed request and stops the loop
options.c: The API keeps the first setting for the whole turn and ignores the rest
options.d: The API silently disables thinking for each altered step and raises no error

explanation.d: The page says the API does not error: it "silently disables thinking for that request".
explanation.b: is ruled out by that same sentence, since the stated behavior is "silently disables thinking for that request" and not a 400.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the changed request is the one that loses thinking: "silently disables thinking for that request".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A tool-use loop is one assistant turn."

quizzes.stem: A team lowers the effort for later turns of a long conversation that relies on a cached document. What follows?

options.a: The stored tools and system are invalidated, but the messages stay valid
options.b: The stored messages are invalidated, so the text is written again
options.c: The cache stays valid, because effort is applied after the prefix
options.d: The cache is invalidated only when the effort is raised above the default

explanation.b: The page says changing the thinking mode or the effort "always discards the cached messages".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the messages are the part that "always discards the cached messages" names, while tools and system are model-specific.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the resolved configuration "is rendered into the prompt", so it is not applied after the prefix.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the messages are discarded on any change: "always discards the cached messages".

quizzes.stem: An agent on Sonnet 5.5 runs at `xhigh` effort, and a developer adds `between_tools` to stop up-front thinking. The request fails. Which statement matches the module?

options.a: The option is valid on Sonnet 5.5 at any effort level
options.b: Each option is valid alone, yet the combination is refused by the API
options.c: The option exists only on Opus models, so any use fails
options.d: The option works only if a manual budget is also sent

explanation.b: The page says "Each setting is valid alone, and the pair returns a 400".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the mode "needs high effort or below".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the table says "skips thinking up front is Sonnet only".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the only budget rule is "A manual budget is at least 1,024", which has no link to this mode.

quizzes.stem: A helpdesk bot prints replies live for agents and also runs overnight bulk jobs. Management wants the speed option on all of it. What does the module say?

options.a: It suits only the watched output, as the batch route excludes it
options.b: It suits neither, since it only lowers time to first token
options.c: It suits neither, because only the cloud platforms offer it
options.d: It suits both, at the standard price for the bulk jobs

explanation.a: The page says "Fast mode is not available with the Batch API." and the speed gain is for output people watch.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Speed benefits are focused on output tokens per second (OTPS), not time to first token (TTFT)."
explanation.c: Ruled out because fast mode "is available on the Claude API (first-party) only".
explanation.d: Ruled out because fast mode carries a premium and "Fast mode is not available with the Batch API."

quizzes.stem: A shared helper serves three Claude models and must never emit a parameter that one of them rejects. What design does the practice use?

options.a: It derives each field from the chosen tier and refuses bad pairs
options.b: It sends one body to every tier and retries whenever the API objects
options.c: It picks the lowest common field and drops the rest silently
options.d: It reads each field from the reply to an earlier call

explanation.a: The practice "turns what an application wants into request parameters for one model" and raises an error for the invalid pairs.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the same sentence says it builds "request parameters for one model", not one shared body.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page warns the API "silently disables thinking for that request", which a silent drop would hide.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The rules are the tables of this module", not a reply.

quizzes.stem: A cost-conscious team wants cheaper answers on Opus 5.5 without losing the cache of a long conversation. Which plan fits?

options.a: Switch to fast mode for the cached turns and standard for the rest
options.b: Change the top-level effort on every second turn and restore it afterward
options.c: Choose the effort level once, before the first turn, and keep it
options.d: Disable thinking after the first answer to cut the output

explanation.c: The page says to choose once per conversation and put what varies after the cached prefix.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "always discards the cached messages".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the table row "Speed setting (fast or standard)" shows system and messages invalidated.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Changing the thinking mode or the effort" is on the invalidation list.
